summary.text: 明 means “bright” or “clear.” Early writing includes a sun-and-moon form associated with brightness or dawn, alongside 朙, a form with the moon and a lattice window associated with moonlight entering a room.

formation.text: 明 has more than one reported early construction. The sun 日 and moon 月 form a celestial image associated with brightness or dawn. A separate form, 朙, combines the moon 月 and window-shaped 囧, picturing moonlight entering through a window; 囧 is also reported as a sound element, though the proposed phonetic role remains disputed.

components.text: In the early 日+月 form, 日 depicts the sun as part of the celestial image associated with brightness or, in one interpretation, dawn.
In the early 日+月 form, 月 depicts the moon as part of the celestial image associated with brightness or, in one interpretation, dawn.

In 朙, 囧 is described as a lattice window and contributes the window image. It is also reported as a sound element, but the phonetic analysis is disputed: the available Old Chinese reconstructions differ from 明 in initial and final, while current Mandarin readings happen to resemble one another; neither comparison establishes the ancient relation or the window’s original spoken name.

sound_limitation.text: The reported phonetic role remains unresolved. The window’s original spoken name is not established, and neither the divergent Old Chinese reconstructions nor the similar current Mandarin readings prove an ancient sound correspondence.

sound.text: In current Mandarin, 囧 is jiǒng and 明 is míng. This modern resemblance is a usable comparison, but it does not establish their ancient sound relationship.
The reported Old Chinese comparison is 囧 *k-mraŋʔ beside 明 *mraŋ in Baxter–Sagart 1.1. The forms differ in initial and final, so this comparison alone does not demonstrate the proposed phonetic role.

components.text: In 朙, 月 depicts the moon in the interpretation of moonlight entering through a window.

history.text: Sun-and-moon forms are reported in oracle-bone and bronze writing. Other reported early forms include 朙, with 月 and 囧, and less secure 目+月 and 田+月 forms. The Shuowen account identifies 明 as an ancient form of 朙; it does not establish 朙 as the sole early construction.
A Qin manuscript’s 目-form is reported as a likely graphic corruption of 囧. This proposed change concerns the written form and does not resolve the relationship among the other early forms.

uncertainties.text: Early examples are reported with both brightness and dawn meanings, but their relative chronology is unresolved. The phonetic analysis of 囧 in 朙 is disputed, and the window’s ancient spoken name is not established.
The reported readings and graphic interpretations of early inscriptions have not been checked against the inscription images; the exact dates of the cited examples are unresolved.

senses.text: Brightness is reported among the uses of oracle-bone examples. The evidence does not show whether this use preceded or followed the attested dawn use.
Dawn is reported among the uses of oracle-bone examples; a line from the Shijing also illustrates daybreak. Its chronological relation to the brightness sense is unresolved.
Clear or manifest uses are reported in bronze inscriptions. How this sense developed from brightness or dawn is not shown.
Current meanings include bright, light, and clear.

limitations.text: The relative chronology of the early brightness and dawn uses, and the development of later clear or manifest uses, remain unresolved.

overview.text: 明 means “bright” or “clear.” Early forms pair the sun and moon, or the moon and a window; these images are associated with brightness, dawn, or moonlight, but do not settle on one original meaning.

components.text: 日 pictures the sun in the early sun-and-moon form.
月 pictures the moon in the early sun-and-moon form.
In 朙, 囧 pictures a lattice window; its proposed sound role remains disputed.
In 朙, 月 pictures the moon in the moonlight-through-a-window interpretation.

relationships.text: In the reported early 日+月 form, 日 depicts the sun as part of the celestial image associated with 明.
In the reported early 日+月 form, 月 depicts the moon as part of the celestial image associated with 明.
The Shuowen account identifies 明 as an ancient form of 朙, whose analysis joins 月 and 囧. This does not show that 朙 was the only early form.
In 朙, 囧 is described as a lattice window and contributes the window image.
In 朙, 月 depicts the moon in the reported moonlight-through-a-window interpretation.

囧 is reported as a sound element in 朙, but the available same-system Old Chinese readings, 囧 *k-mraŋʔ and 明 *mraŋ, differ. Current Mandarin readings jiǒng and míng resemble one another, but do not settle the historical analysis.
